subject: economics
topic: Basic concepts: scarcity, choice, scale of preference and opportunity cost

kept.q: A tailor in Onitsha can use one day to sew either 5 native wears or 3 gowns, since both use the same cloth and machine time. If he decides to sew only gowns for the day, what is his opportunity cost?
options: 5 native wears
3 gowns
8 native wears and gowns combined
The cost of cloth only
kept.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up. Since he chose gowns, what he sacrificed is the 5 native wears he could have sewn instead.
kept.pidgin: Opportunity cost na di next best thing wey person leave. Since di tailor choose gowns, e sacrifice di 5 native wears wey e for fit sew.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why opportunity cost would NOT exist in an economy without scarcity?
options: Without scarcity, all resources would be free goods and choices would not involve giving up alternatives
Without scarcity, prices of goods would simply fall to zero everywhere
Without scarcity, consumers would still rank their wants but choice would remain difficult
Without scarcity, production would increase but opportunity cost would stay constant
kept.explanation: Opportunity cost only arises because resources are limited, forcing a sacrifice when a choice is made. If nothing were scarce, every want could be satisfied without giving up any other want.
kept.pidgin: Opportunity cost dey happen because resources no reach. If everything plenty for ground, we no go need sacrifice one thing to get anoda.

kept.q: Which of the following is the most important factor that forces every household, firm and government to make economic choices?
options: The existence of money as a medium of exchange
The unlimited nature of human wants compared with limited resources
The desire of producers to maximize profit
The presence of competition among sellers in the market
kept.explanation: Choice becomes necessary because human wants are unlimited while the resources available to satisfy them are limited. This mismatch, called scarcity, is the root cause of all economic choices.
kept.pidgin: Choice dey necessary because human wants plenty pass di resources wey we get. Dis scarcity na di main reason why we must dey choose wetin we want.

kept.q: A small-scale fish farmer in Delta State has 100 fingerlings and a pond that can hold either catfish alone, yielding ₦80,000 profit, or tilapia alone, yielding ₦95,000 profit, or a mix of both, yielding ₦70,000 profit. If he decides to go for the mixed option because he wants to reduce risk, what is his opportunity cost?
kept.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone. Since tilapia alone would have given the highest profit of ₦95,000, that is what he sacrifices by choosing the mixed option.
kept.pidgin: Opportunity cost na di value of di best option wey you leave. Since tilapia for give am ₦95,000, na dat money be di cost of im choice.

kept.q: In economics, which of these best distinguishes an economic good from a free good?
options: An economic good is always imported while a free good is always locally produced
An economic good has a price because it is scarce, while a free good has no price because it is abundant relative to demand
An economic good is tangible while a free good is intangible
An economic good is produced by government while a free good is produced by private individuals
kept.explanation: Economic goods are limited in supply relative to human wants, so they command a price. Free goods, such as sunlight or air, are available in such abundance that no one needs to pay for them.
kept.pidgin: Economic goods get price because dem scarce. Free goods like air plenty well-well, so nobody dey pay for dem.

kept.q: A woman weaving aso-oke in Iseyin has 6 hours of daily working time. Weaving one wrapper takes 2 hours and sells for ₦4,000, while weaving one scarf takes 1 hour and sells for ₦1,500. If she uses all 6 hours to weave only scarves instead of only wrappers, what is her opportunity cost in terms of money, assuming she sells everything she produces?
kept.explanation: In 6 hours she can make 3 wrappers worth 3 times ₦4,000 equals ₦12,000, or 6 scarves worth 6 times ₦1,500 equals ₦9,000. By choosing scarves, she gives up the ₦12,000 she would have earned from wrappers, which is her opportunity cost.
kept.pidgin: If she weave wrappers, she go make ₦12,000. Because she choose scarves, she lose dat ₦12,000 wey she for make from wrappers.

q.q: A community development committee in Enugu has ₦2,000,000 to execute only one project this year. They rank their priorities as: (1) borehole, (2) town hall renovation, (3) football pitch, (4) street lights. If the committee eventually executes the town hall renovation instead of the borehole, this decision is best described as evidence of:
options: An inconsistent scale of preference
A reversal of their stated order of priorities
An economic good becoming a free good
A fall in the total wants of the community
q.explanation: The committee had ranked the borehole as first priority, but choosing the town hall renovation instead means they did not follow their stated scale of preference. This shows a reversal of the order they had listed.

q.q: A graduate has ₦600,000 in savings and is considering four uses: (i) start a provision store expected to yield ₦180,000 profit yearly, (ii) buy a car for personal use with no monetary return, (iii) invest in a cooperative society yielding ₦150,000 yearly, (iv) further his education, expected to raise future income by ₦250,000 yearly after graduation. Using purely economic reasoning on returns, how should he arrange these uses on his scale of preference, from most to least preferred?
options: Further education, provision store, cooperative society, car
Car, further education, provision store, cooperative society
Provision store, further education, car, cooperative society
Cooperative society, car, provision store, further education
q.explanation: A scale of preference based on returns ranks options by expected benefit from highest to lowest. Further education gives the highest return (₦250,000), followed by the store (₦180,000), then the cooperative (₦150,000), while the car gives no monetary return and comes last.

rejected.why: ambiguous:Delayed returns are not directly comparable with immediate annual returns.|
